newsitem.title: BRAZIL: INTERVIEW - Brazil's Bozano moves to expand overseas.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Brazil's Bozano moves to expand overseas.

text.p: Brazilian investment bank Banco Bozano, Simonsen has hammered out a strategy to expand abroad in coming years, including opening offices in countries from Latin America to Asia, the bank's president said.

Bank chief Paulo Ferraz said the bank plans to open a Singapore office in the second half of 1997, two or three new broker dealers in the U.S. in 1998 and another brokerage in Asia, probably Japan, in the future.
Bozano already has brokerages in New York and London. The London brokerage has just opened for business.
"We want to be close to the client who is interested in Brazil," he told Reuters in a telephone interview.

Foreign interest in Brazil, the region's largest economy, has surged since the nearly three-year-old Real stabilization plan tamed inflation and restored the country's financial credibility in global markets.
Bozano would be the first Brazilian investment bank to embark on a truly global expansion.
In Latin America, it will begin by opening a representative office in Argentina in a month, turning it into an investment bank within one year.
"The idea is to do investment banking in the rest of Latin America as we do here," Ferraz said, adding that Bozano will then move on to Chile, Venezuela, Colombia, Peru, Uruguay and Mexico.
With the opening of investment banks in Latin America and the brokerages worldwide, Bozano will be able to offer business opportunities in the region to investors, instead of Brazil alone, he added.
"Many investors look at the region as a whole and not only Brazil," he said.

Bozano, Simonsen has been active in all areas of investment banking, including capital markets, asset management and corporate finance. It manages $5 billion in client assets, of which around $3.5 billion in foreign investment, Ferraz said.
Bozano has also played a key role in Brazil's privatizations as an investors' advisor.

Currently, the bank is advising South Africa's Anglo-American which joined forces with local cement, steel, pulp and paper group Grupo Votorantim to bid at the April 29 privatization auction of state mining concern Companhia Vale do Rio Doce.
It is also taking part in consortia which are competing to advise on the sale of Sao Paulo state power utilities.
Since early 1996, Bozano has been in charge of preparing Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj for privatization.
Bozano bank is part of Bozano, Simonsen Group which has interests in 30 companies in industrial, agricultural and real estate businesses, with consolidated assets of over $6.0 billion.

Bozano group led the country's first privatizations, by acquiring stakes in steel firms Usiminas, Companhia Siderurgica de Tubarao and Cosipa, power utility Escelsa and aircraft manufacturer Embraer .
Now it only holds stakes in Cosipa and Embraer.
